slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 26:2-5: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky...and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed.
slides.body: “I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky...and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed.”
slides.heading: Gen 26:2-5

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the claim that Genesis 26 promises the Redeemer through Isaac.
slides.body: Genesis renews Abraham's promises through Isaac. Hebrews recalls that Isaac's line must continue. Christian lists sometimes say these verses promise Jesus as Redeemer.
slides.heading: Was Isaac's offspring promised as the Redeemer?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the broader canonical Christian promise trajectory.
slides.body: Land, countless descendants and worldwide blessing pass through Isaac. Galatians later centres the Abrahamic promise in Christ. Across the whole canon, Jesus can be presented as the line's redemptive culmination.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three explains the incorrect proof-text mapping and added Redeemer language.
slides.body: Genesis promises a multitude, not one identified saviour. Hebrews 11:18 quotes Genesis 21:12—not Genesis 26—and discusses Abraham's faith that Isaac's family line would survive. The explicit christological identification comes from elsewhere.
slides.heading: The citations don't say ‘Redeemer’

title: Does Genesis call Isaac's descendant the Redeemer?
